action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the currently attached simulator, or the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

1	# Codex red-team — local experimental port with observable verification
2	
3	## Context — the gap / problem
4	
5	The operator wants a lightweight standalone local Codex red-team plugin, delivered like Snipe. It should retain red-team's adversarial purpose while allowing instruction and behavior experiments, declared deviations, and iterative repair. Complete Claude–Codex alignment is deferred; the comparison itself is intended to inform that later alignment. (user)
6	
7	The development baseline is `origin/codex-port`, observed at `9bc8f676fac1794838f556ed74f2c0d1a9b7bac5` on 2026-09-08. PR #2152 is OPEN and draft. The local root checkout is an older, dirty `master`; it must not supply this migration's base. Refresh the remote reference and record the selected baseline at handoff rather than assuming this observed SHA is still current. (verified: PR #2152 metadata and local git refs on 2026-09-08)
8	
9	The maintained red-team has a Workflow scaffold, an independent verdict gate, an escape guard, and Lead-driven source intake, probe derivation, adjudication, and report duties. Its scope-lock fingerprint is not an exact plan-content or repository-revision identity. The immutable aggregate preserves post-confirmation results; it does not preserve every pre-confirmation finding. (verified: `skills/red-team/SKILL.md`, `assets/workflow-scaffold.js` constructs `runProbe`, `confirmStage` and final return, and `assets/red-team-gate.mjs` at the observed baseline)
10	
11	Issue #1848 records a recommendation contradicted by operator comments omitted from issue intake. Issue #1919 includes red-team's living prose. Issue #2097 supplies repeated repair-loop observations and later qualifications: class-wide reasoning and independent evidence are useful hypotheses, but the early estimate of rounds saved is not causal proof. (verified: issues #1848, #1919 and #2097, full bodies and comments fetched 2026-09-08)

37	
38	- Start development and comparison preparation from the current `codex-port`, retaining its existing Codex code; exclude the new red-team migration from comparison starting branches. (user)

52	| Experiments | Explicit deviations, hypotheses and proposed tests are required; observations may refute them | PIN-6 · (user) | guardrail |
53	| Implementation ledger | Keep a detailed contemporaneous ledger through implementation and audit/repair cycles | PIN-7 · (user) | slice (T1, T2, T3) |
54	| Independent comparison | Review frozen inputs independently before revealing implementation history or peer findings | PIN-8 · (user) | backstop |
55	| Comparison branch topology | Two independent review branches and PRs target a third comparison branch; original master-base instruction superseded by PIN-11 | PIN-9 · (user) | context |
56	| Authoring delivery | After plan confirmation, author creates branches, commits plan/instructions and opens both comparison PRs; does not merge or launch reviews | PIN-10 · (user) | context |
57	| Corrected branch base | All three branches start from the same current codex-port SHA, preserving existing Codex implementation but excluding this migration | PIN-11 · (user) | guardrail |
58	| Distribution | Lightweight standalone local-only, following Snipe's delivery approach | PIN-12 · (user) | end-state |
59	| Mechanism latitude | Prompts, references, lenses, scheduling, runner internals and bounded retry/round settings may change within the outcome floor | PIN-13 · (user) | guardrail |

64	**Verifier decisions retained.** Sol/low is the interview verifier profile, not a future red-team default. Complete shared-content inventory was declined after two refutations; its omission risk is accepted and deferred under PIN-5. Manual independent-review ordering was accepted despite its lack of technical blinding enforcement. The latitude review found evidence-intake and zero-attempt holes: complete intake is explicit, initial attempts cannot be disabled by retry settings, and vacuity remains observable. The operator permits an imperfect first installed run, never an invented success. No verifier dispatch was waived. The decomposition verifier also proposed cross-phase task deps; source inspection contradicts that recommendation: `skills/war/SKILL.md` dispatches one Workflow per phase, and the engine initializes `succeeded` per invocation. This plan keeps separate sequential phases with empty intra-phase deps; the operator confirmed that source-based rebuttal at Echo-back 1. No new Snipe cleanup repair is assumed solely because #2235 remains open. (user; [assumed: other listed scope exclusions keep this migration bounded — if wrong: reopen scope before implementation])

80	## New domain terms · Recommended ADRs
81	
82	**Vacuous run:** a run presented as verification without meaningful coverage of its declared review obligations. Zero findings alone do not establish vacuity: a legitimate clean review may have no findings, and an applicable plan may require analyzed probes only. Distinguish zero dispatches, missing/off-target results, failed confirmations, and evidence too weak to support the advertised claim. This is a scoped operational definition, not a claim that semantic vacuity can be fully decided by code. [assumed: working definition for this experiment — if wrong: refine from observed runs without hiding them]
83	
84	**Experiment record:** declared baseline → deviation → prediction → test → observation → retain/revise/revert/pending. **Implementation incident:** symptom → hypothesis/verified cause → attempts → decisions → evidence → residuals. Reuse existing vocabulary elsewhere. No ADR creation is required now; recommend a later ADR only if a tested experiment becomes a lasting cross-host contract. [assumed: scoped vocabulary and no present irreversible architecture decision — if wrong: recommend an ADR at alignment]

86	## Commander's Intent
87	
88	- **Purpose:** Give Codex a useful adversarial red-team for plans, and use this migration to learn which instruction and behavior changes improve it.
89	- **Method:** Ship a lightweight local standalone plugin; reuse what works, experiment explicitly, include the red-team portions of #1848 and #1919, apply lessons from #2097, and preserve a detailed implementation ledger. Compare independent Codex and Claude reviews of this original plan with implementation pain points after installation.
90	- **Mechanism latitude:** Prompt wording, reference layout, role/lens organization, scheduling, runtime internals and bounded retry/round policy are implementer's choice. Begin from the existing behavior, record each departure and its hypothesis/test before applying it, and preserve observations afterward. Substituting any of these mechanisms while the End states and binding guardrails hold is not a plan deviation and warrants no issue. An experimental departure is still recorded in the ledger; that record is not automatically a follow-up issue.
91	- **Binding guardrails:** PIN-6 and PIN-13 require declared testable deviations without waiving End states, checks or backstops. Probes do not mutate target source or perform outward push/deploy/send actions; analyzed roles are read-only, execution occurs in disposable isolated environments, and Lead writes stay within the authorized plan/report/evidence scope. Preserve independent adversarial confirmation, operator decision authority, truthful evidence/coverage/adjudication reporting, finite failure handling, and no silent capability or profile widening. Issue evidence includes full bodies/comments and accounted-for linked artifacts or explicit access gaps. PIN-11 fixes comparison branch ancestry to one current codex-port commit, with no new migration implementation on those starting branches. Complete alignment is deliberately not a guardrail.

# Codex red-team — local experimental port with observable verification

## Context — the gap / problem

The operator wants a lightweight standalone local Codex red-team plugin, delivered like Snipe. It should retain red-team's adversarial purpose while allowing instruction and behavior experiments, declared deviations, and iterative repair. Complete Claude–Codex alignment is deferred; the comparison itself is intended to inform that later alignment. (user)

The development baseline is `origin/codex-port`, observed at `9bc8f676fac1794838f556ed74f2c0d1a9b7bac5` on 2026-09-08. PR #2152 is OPEN and draft. The local root checkout is an older, dirty `master`; it must not supply this migration's base. Refresh the remote reference and record the selected baseline at handoff rather than assuming this observed SHA is still current. (verified: PR #2152 metadata and local git refs on 2026-09-08)

The maintained red-team has a Workflow scaffold, an independent verdict gate, an escape guard, and Lead-driven source intake, probe derivation, adjudication, and report duties. Its scope-lock fingerprint is not an exact plan-content or repository-revision identity. The immutable aggregate preserves post-confirmation results; it does not preserve every pre-confirmation finding. (verified: `skills/red-team/SKILL.md`, `assets/workflow-scaffold.js` constructs `runProbe`, `confirmStage` and final return, and `assets/red-team-gate.mjs` at the observed baseline)

Issue #1848 records a recommendation contradicted by operator comments omitted from issue intake. Issue #1919 includes red-team's living prose. Issue #2097 supplies repeated repair-loop observations and later qualifications: class-wide reasoning and independent evidence are useful hypotheses, but the early estimate of rounds saved is not causal proof. (verified: issues #1848, #1919 and #2097, full bodies and comments fetched 2026-09-08)

**Verifier decisions retained.** Sol/low is the interview verifier profile, not a future red-team default. The operator permits an imperfect first installed run, never an invented success. No verifier dispatch was waived. The decomposition verifier also proposed cross-phase task deps; source inspection contradicts that recommendation: `skills/war/SKILL.md` dispatches one Workflow per phase, and the engine initializes `succeeded` per invocation. This plan keeps separate sequential phases with empty intra-phase deps; the operator confirmed that source-based rebuttal at Echo-back 1. (user; verified: retained interview verifier results and named phase-dispatch constructs at the observed baseline)

## Assumptions ledger

322	const runProbe = (p) => dispatchAgent(
323	  `${scopeLock(p.technique)}\n\n${futureWorkRule(p.technique, artifactKind)}\n\n${p.prompt}\n\nReturn ONLY the FINDINGS object (probe="${p.name}", kind="${p.kind}", technique="${p.technique}"). Prove any failure with reproduced evidence; never assert. Set needsDecision:true on any finding that is an ambiguity with more than one non-equivalent resolution — a hole only the user can settle. Only record a finding for an actual problem — a false claim, a gap, or an ambiguity (needsDecision). If a claim checks out, do NOT record it. A fully-clean probe returns status:"pass" with findings:[].`,
324	  { ...modelOpts, label: `probe:${p.name}`, phase: 'Probe',
325	    agentType: p.technique === 'analyzed' ? ANALYZED_AGENT : undefined, schema: FINDINGS })
326	
327	const confirmStage = async (res, p) => {               // adversarial-confirm: refute any reproducible blocker
328	  const blocking = res && (res.findings || []).some(f => f.severity === 'Critical' || f.severity === 'Major')
329	  if (!res || (res.status !== 'fail' && !blocking)) return res
330	  const c = await dispatchAgent(
331	    `${scopeLock(p.technique)}\n\n`
332	    + `Independently try to REFUTE this red-team finding — reproduce it or disprove it. `
333	    + `Apply the self-confound gate to the probe itself: rule out the probe's own provision commands, sandbox reuse, or an earlier probe's mutation as the cause before the fail stands. `
334	    + `Work ONLY in a throwaway sandbox; never touch ${repo}.\nProbe: ${p.name}\nPlan: ${planFile}\n`
335	    + `Findings: ${JSON.stringify(res.findings)}`,
336	    { ...modelOpts, label: `${ADVERSARIAL_CONFIRM}:${p.name}`, phase: 'Confirm',
337	      agentType: p.technique === 'analyzed' ? ANALYZED_AGENT : undefined, schema: CONFIRM })
338	  if (c && c.reproduced === false) {
339	    return { ...res, status: 'warn',
340	      findings: (res.findings || []).map(f => ({ ...f, severity: 'Minor',
341	        reality: `${f.reality || ''} [unreproduced — downgraded by ${ADVERSARIAL_CONFIRM}: ${c.note || ''}]` })) }
342	  }
343	  return res
344	}
345	
346	const results = await pipeline(allProbes, runProbe, confirmStage)
347	
348	// Layer 4 — never silently drop a dead probe. A null = the agent died after the harness's own
349	// retries (or was skipped). Retry it ONCE; if it still dies, emit a { probe, dropped:true } marker
350	// so the gate counts the coverage gap and refuses to return CLEARED on a thinner run.
351	const probeResults = []
352	for (let i = 0; i < allProbes.length; i++) {
353	  let r = results[i]
354	  if (!r) {
355	    log(`Probe ${allProbes[i].name} returned no result — retrying once.`)
356	    const retried = await pipeline([allProbes[i]], runProbe, confirmStage)
357	    r = retried[0]
358	  }
359	  // Provenance strip (ADR 0043): the `adjudicated` stamp is Lead-applied post-run only, in the
360	  // Lead's working copy of the gate input — a probe has no legitimate path to it, so the key is
361	  // deleted from every finding of every collected result at this single site right before the push
362	  // (first-pass and retried results alike). One key only: findings without it pass by reference,
363	  // the dropped:true markers and the confirm-stage reality suffix (a declared key) are untouched.
364	  if (r && Array.isArray(r.findings)) {
365	    r = { ...r, findings: r.findings.map(f => {
366	      if (!f || typeof f !== 'object' || !('adjudicated' in f)) return f
367	      const { adjudicated, ...keep } = f
368	      return keep
369	    }) }
370	  }
371	  probeResults.push(r || { probe: allProbes[i].name, dropped: true })
372	}
373	const dropped = probeResults.filter(r => r && r.dropped).map(r => r.probe)
374	if (dropped.length) log(`⚠ coverage gap: ${dropped.length}/${allProbes.length} probe(s) dropped after retry — ${dropped.join(', ')}. The gate will return INCOMPLETE.`)
375	
376	return { plan: planFile, repo, fingerprint, provision, expected: allProbes.length, probeResults }

1	# Red Team — lenses, probes, schemas, report
2	
3	## Spine lenses (always run)
4	The six universal lenses live in [`../assets/workflow-scaffold.js`](../assets/workflow-scaffold.js) (`SPINE`):
5	- **claims-vs-reality** — every concrete claim (file/symbol/signature/line/"before" snippet) checked against the live repo.
6	- **executable-proof** — every test/command/edit the plan ships is run in a sandbox; assert it matches the stated "Expected".
7	- **coverage-vs-source** — every requirement in the source spec/issue maps to a plan step; unmapped = Major gap. Merged arm: when the source IS the plan itself (Part 1 carries the decision record — the plan is its own source of truth; `--spec` defaults to the plan), the lens reads Part-1→Part-2 coverage: every Part-1 requirement/decision maps to a Part-2 phase/task. Per-issue Evidence join (merged arm only): when the plan carries an Evidence-consumed block, join it against each cited source issue's `## Evidence artifacts` section — every artifact the issue lists must appear in the block as read or unread-with-reason; a listed artifact the block omits is the gap. Split absence arms: an issue whose `## Evidence artifacts` section is absent ⇒ the join is **vacuous** for that issue (the `touched-doc-fact-coverage` vacuity pattern — nothing to join is a pass, not a finding); an issue that is **unreachable** (gh/network/auth failure, incl. an exogenous account flip) ⇒ a **named unverified note** identifying that issue in the report — never silent, never vacuous.
8	- **consistency-placeholders** — TBD/TODO/vague steps, name/signature drift, contradictions.
9	- **dependency-feasibility** — assumed interfaces/deps/tools exist; ordering is sound.
10	- **intent-vs-plan** — fires on either intent heading (`## Commander's Intent` or `## AI-Commander's Intent`): each End-state condition individually checkable (else Major) and mapped to ≥1 claiming phase (else Major); collectively sufficient for the Purpose (else Major `needsDecision`). An `## AI-Commander's Intent` block is intent-present and judged identically, plus one Minor note recommending the human upgrade path (`/war-strategy <plan>`); a plan with **neither** heading passes with a Minor note recommending the intent interview — never Major.
11	
12	## Drift-guard spine probes (run every red-team)
13	Four universal doctrine probes the Lead runs on every plan (vacuous when the plan has no matching feature; none skipped under `--fast`), enforcing ADR 0025's drift-guard discipline. **Not** members of the `SPINE` array — Lead-run like the backstop-legitimacy check (see [backstop-legitimacy.md](backstop-legitimacy.md)):
14	- **`unguarded-new-mirror`** — analyzed. Every new inline mirror of a canonical export a plan adds (a `const` in `workflow-template.js` re-declaring `HARD_ESCALATION_REASONS` / a `landDecision` set / a roster helper) must ship a matching **mirror-registry** row in `workflow-template.test.mjs` in the same task; a mirror with no row is a plan defect (`needsDecision`). Prove by grepping the plan's file list — an added `const` with no registry-row edit in the same task is the fail.
15	- **`default-flip-old-absent`** — executed. Every default-flip / scope-narrow task's gate must assert the OLD value **absent** across every enumerated surface, not just NEW-present. Prove in a sandbox: leave one stale surface carrying the old value and run the gate; a still-green gate is the defect (`NEW-present` alone is the recorded failure mode).
16	- **`guard-split-deps-edge`** — analyzed. Every drift guard a plan authors must ride in the **same task** as the fact it guards, or — when split into a different task of the same phase — carry a `deps` edge onto the task authoring that fact; **same wave is insufficient**, because every task worktree is cut from one frozen phase base, so the split guard is red by construction at its own base. Scope is wider than `unguarded-new-mirror`: *any* split drift guard counts — prose mirrors and doc-guard tests included, not only inline `const` mirrors. Prove by reading the plan's per-task `Files:`/`deps:` lists — a guard task with no `deps` edge onto the fact-authoring task is the fail (`needsDecision`), grilled until the plan adds the edge, merges the two tasks, or moves the guard a phase later. Vacuous when the plan splits no guard away from its fact; not skipped under `--fast` (ADR 0025 Consequences).
17	- **`touched-doc-fact-coverage`** — analyzed. Every task whose `Files:` rewrites a doc must show the **guard / de-mirror / defer** choice for each fact the doc renders authoritative that is derivable from a machine-readable in-repo source (a config default, a manifest field, an enum member, a version slot — never prose claims generally): a **guard** (drift test binding the doc value to its source by extraction + equality), a **de-mirror** (the doc points at the canonical source instead of restating its value), or an **explicit defer** (a legitimacy-complete `## Deferred validations (backstops)` row naming runner + timing — never a prose waiver). Prove by reading the plan's per-task `Files:` lists and slices — a doc-rewriting task restating such a fact with none of the three is the fail (`needsDecision`), grilled until the plan guards, de-mirrors, or explicitly defers. Vacuous when no task rewrites a doc or the touched docs carry no such facts; not skipped under `--fast` (ADR 0025's touched-doc amendment; authoring twin: `/war-strategy` §3 rule 8).
18	
19	## Bespoke probe catalog (derive from the plan's features)
20	Add one probe per matching feature (edit the scaffold's array or pass `args.probes`):
21	
22	| Plan feature | Probe `name` | `technique` | Prompt gist |
23	|---|---|---|---|
24	| before/after edit snippet | `snippet-fidelity` | analyzed | "Confirm each **anchor/'before'** snippet (the text an edit attaches to) appears VERBATIM in the live file; report drift + the actual text. The plan's proposed **after**-state is its deliverable — EXPECTED absent, **never** report it." |
25	| code block + test block | `tests-run` | executed | "Extract the module + test to a temp dir, run the test runner, report the pass/fail counts." |
26	| shell command + expected output | `command-diff` | executed | "Run the command in a sandbox; diff actual vs the stated Expected." |
27	| cited line numbers | `anchor-check` | analyzed | "Confirm each cited line number points where the plan says." |
28	| "no X → today's behavior" baseline | `baseline-repro` | executed | "Reproduce the baseline in a sandbox and confirm the claimed equivalence." |
29	| new dependency / tool | `dep-resolves` | executed | "Confirm the dep/tool resolves or installs in a sandbox." |
30	| multi-file edit ordering | `edits-compose` | executed | "Apply all edits to a scratch copy in order; confirm they compose and the result builds." |
31	| per-task merge-commit anchor (`<merge>^1`, `--first-parent` per-task diff, post-merge three-dot floor base) | `ff-topology` | executed | "In a **fresh `git init` synthetic repo** (never a copy of `repo` — nothing in `repo` is read or run), build WAR's real integration topology: base commit → integration branch → ≥2 'task' integrations done as **fast-forward** merges (a linear single-parent chain — NO per-task merge commit) → one final `--no-ff` phase-land merge. Then evaluate EVERY plan clause that anchors per-task evidence on merge topology against that fixture: a clause that errors, resolves the wrong commit (`^1` on a single-parent tip walks to the previous commit, under-populating the changed-file set), or degenerates to an empty diff (post-merge `<integration>...<task>` is always empty once the task tip is an ancestor) is **topology-void** → Major, with the fixture output as evidence. **Provision-exempt:** build and evaluate the fixture even if repo provisioning failed or was skipped — this probe never touches the repo copy, so a provision failure never converts it to warn-and-skip. **Vacuous pass:** if on reading the plan no clause actually anchors per-task evidence on merge topology (a false-positive token trigger — e.g. `^1` inside an unrelated code block), return `status:\"pass\"` with `findings:[]` — never invent a clause to evaluate." |
32	
33	For a plan with **no runnable artifacts** (a design doc/PRD), drop the executed probes; coverage, consistency, feasibility, and ambiguity (`needsDecision`) carry the verification.
34	The **`ff-topology`** row is **mandatory when triggered** and **`--fast`-proof** (it mirrors the SKILL.md Step 2 rule; the presence-pair guard in [`../assets/workflow-scaffold.test.mjs`](../assets/workflow-scaffold.test.mjs) pins the pair). It takes **precedence over** the no-runnable-artifacts executed-drop above: its fixture is a self-contained synthetic repo, so a `design-doc`/`prd` that anchors on per-task merge topology still runs it.
35	
36	## Scope-lock, attestation & coverage (foreign-cwd defense)
37	`/red-team` is routinely launched from project X's session to verify project Y's plan (`--repo` ≠ cwd). A probe agent's ambient cwd + CLAUDE.md + memory **overpower** explicit path args, so prevention alone is insufficient (drift survived absolute paths in the 2026-06-19 incident). The hardening is defense-in-depth:
38	- **Scope-lock preamble** — the scaffold prepends a hard preamble to **every** probe (spine *and* bespoke) and confirm: ignore the session cwd, the only subject is the fingerprinted plan + `repo`, executed probes work in a throwaway *copy* of `repo`, analyzed probes restrict reads to `repo`, and STOP if the opened plan's title differs. **Bespoke probe authors:** you get this for free, but still write your gist to name the absolute `repo`/`planFile`.
39	- **Provision step (executed probes)** — when the Lead passes a `provision` list (the pinned, repo-derived setup commands — see Part B's `provision.mjs` / setup-scout), the scope-lock additionally directs every **executed** probe to run those commands **in the sandbox copy, before the baseline**, bringing the tree to a gate-ready state (submodules, dependency install, …). Provisioning is environment setup, not the artifact under test: a **failing** provision step is an env-gap → `status:"warn"` + a note, and is **never** a red/fail verdict (a broken environment must not be mis-scored as a broken plan). Stamp the note finding `envGap: true`; the gate demotes it to a Minor note (`../assets/red-team-gate.mjs` `classify()`), so the enforcement is gate-side and typed, not prompt-trust alone. An empty/absent list adds nothing (back-compat); analyzed read-only probes never provision.
40	- **Anchor attestation** — every probe must report `read_anchor` (what it read); the gate discards off-target results. This is the layer that catches drift even when the preamble fails.
41	- **`INCOMPLETE` verdict** — the gate returns `CLEARED | CLEARED-WITH-NOTES | ADJUDICATED | BLOCKED | INCOMPLETE`. `INCOMPLETE` whenever a probe was off-target, dropped, or never ran; the gate **never** returns `CLEARED` on incomplete coverage, and `INCOMPLETE` outranks every other arm including `ADJUDICATED`. The Lead re-runs the off-target/dropped probes before any other verdict can settle.
42	- **Pre/post ref-diff escape guard (executed probes)** — the Lead runs [`../assets/assert-no-repo-escape.sh`](../assets/assert-no-repo-escape.sh) twice: `--repo <repo> --snapshot <abs-file>` immediately before launching the Workflow (an absolute path outside the target's tree; exit 1 there means residue or dirt **predates** this run and must be resolved, never baselined over; pre-existing gitignored residue is the exception — it is recorded in the snapshot, never refused), and `--repo <repo> --baseline <that file>` after it returns and before the gate (0 = clean; 1 = an escape — a stray working-tree file, a **new non-allowlisted gitignored file** measured against the snapshot's recorded ignored file set (including a new file inside a directory the snapshot already listed files under), a junk sandbox ref, or any `refs/heads/`/`refs/tags/` ref added, removed, or SHA-moved since the snapshot; 2 = a git/infra error or unreadable or zero-byte baseline, never a pass). Without `--baseline` the ref half is only the junk-**name** heuristic that a probe-invented name slips, and the gitignored half does not run at all. An exit 1 routes the verdict through the self-confound gate, **action-provenance first** ([../SKILL.md](../SKILL.md) Step 4): a probe-authored or unresolved delta is a real escape and forbids `CLEARED` until containment re-runs the guard clean *with* `--baseline`, while a delta cleared as foreign — another session's or worktree's ref in a shared ref store, or an ignored file another session wrote inside the window — is recorded and does not block `CLEARED` (an ignored path of unsettled provenance is moved aside, never deleted); an exit 2 carries no delta to triage — fix the named git/infra fault and re-run the guard. Both nonzero codes forbid `CLEARED` until the guard is settled. So a probe that escaped its sandbox (the recorded cwd-reset / bare-push shape) is caught by **detection** even when the SCOPE-LOCK **prevention** preamble failed. This is the ratified replacement for the previously-deferred execution harness (ADR 0033); a full probe-confinement jail was a rejected non-goal — the post-run guard closes the trust gap without one.
43	
44	## Schemas
45	`FINDINGS` (per probe) and `CONFIRM` (per adversarial-confirm) are defined in the scaffold. `FINDINGS` has a **required** `read_anchor: { resolved_path, plan_title }` — what the probe ACTUALLY read; the gate validates it against the run's **fingerprint** (`{ absPath, titleLine, tokens }`, computed by the Lead from the absolute `planFile` and passed in `args.fingerprint`). A probe whose `read_anchor` does not match the fingerprint is **off-target**: its findings are discarded and it counts as a coverage failure. Shape of a finding:
46	```jsonc
47	{ severity: "Critical" | "Major" | "Minor",
48	  needsDecision: false,          // true = a hole to grill the user on
49	  deliverableAbsence: false,     // true ONLY when the 'absent' symbol is mapped by coverage-vs-source to a plan task — the gate never blocks on it
50	  adjudicated: false,            // Lead-stamped at grill time (never probe-set): this blocker/needsDecision is patched but not re-verified. Typed, strict === true; scanned only over the blockers+needsDecision union, so an unstamped Minor never holds the verdict
51	  claim: "what the plan asserts",
52	  reality: "what red-team found",
53	  evidence: "reproduced proof — error output, diff, transcript",
54	  fix: "suggested resolution",
55	  planRef: "Task/Step/line" }
56	```
57	
58	**Precondition vs deliverable (analyzed probes — shared `preconditionRule` in the scaffold).** A plan *proposes* changes; it has not run. Analyzed probes verify only that the plan's **preconditions** hold against the live repo (the anchor/insertion-point text each edit attaches to exists verbatim, assumed-existing files/symbols/signatures are present, the edits would apply and compose). The plan's proposed new code, new tests, comment edits, and version bumps are its **deliverable** — expected absent, so their finding-shape splits two ways:
59	- **precondition-missing → a real finding** (a missing/renamed anchor, a false claim about *existing* code, a wrong signature, a drifted line number, an internal contradiction, edits that would not compose).
60	- **after-state-not-yet-present → NEVER a finding** ("the proposed line/version/test isn't in the repo yet" — that is the expected pre-execution baseline, not a defect).
61	
62	**Artifact-kind grading (all probes — `futureWorkRule` in the scaffold, ADR 0032).** The precondition/deliverable split above generalizes across probe modes by **`artifactKind`** (`impl-plan` / `tdd-plan` / `design-doc` / `prd`; the Lead classifies it in the pre-flight and threads it in `args.artifactKind` — see [../SKILL.md](../SKILL.md) Step 2; absent ⇒ `impl-plan`, the suppression-safe default). For an `impl-plan` or `tdd-plan`, a claimed-but-unbuilt symbol / test / file is the expected deliverable baseline — **never a finding** — on **executed** probes too, not just analyzed ones; for a `tdd-plan` specifically, a shipped test running **red pre-implementation is `status:"pass"`**, not a defect. The retained-findings carve-out is unchanged: a false claim about *existing* code, a missing anchor, a wrong signature, a drifted line, or an internal contradiction still blocks.
63	
64	**Deliverable-absence flag (`deliverableAbsence` on a finding).** A probe sets `deliverableAbsence: true` **only** when the 'absent' symbol it flags is mapped by `coverage-vs-source` to a plan task (the plan promises to add it). The gate never counts a `deliverableAbsence:true` finding as a blocker, regardless of severity or probe status — it keys on the typed flag alone, doing no `reality`-string parsing (the gate stays pure). This kills the recorded 16-false-findings `BLOCKED` misfire at the gate layer.
65	
66	## Severity & gate (enforced by [`../assets/red-team-gate.mjs`](../assets/red-team-gate.mjs))
67	- **Critical** — provably false in a way that breaks execution (test fails, edit won't apply, file/symbol absent). Blocks **only when the parent probe's `status` is not `"pass"`** (i.e. `warn`, `fail`, or absent). A Critical from a `status:"pass"` probe is a confirmation artifact, not a defect — it does not block.
68	- **Major** — real defect or coverage gap → wrong/incomplete results. Same status-aware rule: blocks only when probe `status !== "pass"`.
69	- **Minor** — cosmetic/robustness. Auto-note; auto-fix when unambiguous. Not affected by probe status.
70	- **`needsDecision`** — an underspecified hole (an ambiguity with >1 non-equivalent resolution) → grill the user, at any severity. **Always blocks, regardless of probe `status`.** Probe agents set `needsDecision:true` on any such finding.
71	- **Verdict:** `CLEARED` (no blockers/holes/minors) · `CLEARED-WITH-NOTES` (minors only) · `ADJUDICATED` (every open blocker/hole is patched and Lead-stamped, at least one of them; distinct from a clear — no probe re-proof was run) · `BLOCKED` (an open blocker/hole carrying no stamp) · `INCOMPLETE` (coverage gap — an off-target, dropped, or never-ran probe; re-run before any other verdict).
72	
73	> **Two-contract summary.** (1) *Probe side* — a finding is a DEFECT only; claims that check out are NOT recorded; a clean probe returns `status:"pass"` with `findings:[]`. (2) *Gate side* — `probeStatus !== "pass"` (warn/fail/absent) still blocks for Critical/Major; `needsDecision` always blocks; only literal `"pass"` demotes a Critical/Major to non-blocker.
74	>
75	> _Pinned by the **D7 drift-guard** in [`../assets/red-team-gate.test.mjs`](../assets/red-team-gate.test.mjs): it asserts this two-contract sentence is present in both this file and the CONTRACTS comment in [`../assets/workflow-scaffold.js`](../assets/workflow-scaffold.js), and that `'pass'` is the **only** status demoting a Critical/Major — removing either surface, or widening the demoting set, turns the guard red._
76	
77	## Report template → `docs/red-team/YYYY-MM-DD-<plan-slug>.md`
78	```markdown
79	# Red Team — <plan> (<date>)
80	**Verdict:** CLEARED | CLEARED-WITH-NOTES | ADJUDICATED | BLOCKED | INCOMPLETE — <one line>
81	**Rounds:** <integer>
82	<!-- Cumulative grill sweeps: the Step-1 seed + this run's sweeps. Strict form — the next run's seeding re-reads exactly this line; an integer, nothing else. -->
83	
84	## Attack surface
85	Spine: <6 lenses>. Bespoke: <probes run>. Executed in sandbox: <which>.
86	Fallback: <none | analyzed-agent fallback engaged (sticky pin); probes run on general-purpose: names from the dispatchedOn/fallbackEngaged result stamps>.
87	
88	## Executed proof
89	- <what ran> → <result, e.g. "tests 20/20 green on Node v26"; "10/10 edits apply">
90	
91	## Findings
92	### Critical / Major / Minor
93	- [<severity>] <claim> → <reality>. Evidence: <…>. Resolution: <patch applied / accepted>.
94	
95	## Resolutions applied (grill decisions)
96	- <finding> → <decision> → <plan ref patched>
97	
98	## Adjudications
99	<!-- Machine-readable: the WAR Lead reads these rows and threads them into the auditor prompts (auditPrompt() and the gate-audit seats). Version precedence: task instruction > red-team adjudication > plan body literal. Leave empty (or omit) when no authoritative value was adjudicated — an empty block is byte-identical no-op for the auditor.
100	     Every row carries its OWN provenance token — `operator-ratified (<date>)` or `AI-declared` — never a block-level marker: one run can mix operator rulings with Lead self-adjudication (--afk) in the same report (ADR 0014's heading-level provenance, taken to per-row grain; ADR 0043 Decision 5).
101	     Carve-out granularity, when a row excludes a registry/both-surfaces-pinned span from a shrink: THE EXTRACTION'S READ IS THE CARVE-OUT — it covers exactly the bytes that row's drift-guard extraction actually reads. Ordered/positional-key regions are atomic; unread residue stays shrink-eligible; the rationale is bounded to runtime prompt strings and never transfers to a standing-doc card span. See docs/adr/0043-adjudicated-clear-distinct-terminal-verdict.md § Carve-out granularity. -->
102	- <adjudicated literal> supersedes <plan-body literal it replaces> — <plan ref / reason> — <operator-ratified (<date>) | AI-declared>
103	
104	## Residual risk
105	- <minor notes / accepted assumptions>
106	
107	## Route upstream
108	<!-- Only on a route-upstream terminal (gate emitted `routeUpstream: true`); omit otherwise. Doctrine + block template: skills/red-team/references/loop-budget.md. -->
109	**Regrill:** `/war-strategy <abs plan path>` — run the interview on the agenda below; it patches the plan.
110	**Agenda (residual questions):**
111	- <the unsettled decision — its non-equivalent resolutions, and what the gate saw>
112	
113	**Re-entry:** `/red-team <abs plan path> [--repo <path>]` — after the regrill; the fresh run seeds its cumulative count from this report's `**Rounds:**` line.
114	```
115	
116	## Safety
117	- Never mutate the repo's source or run the plan against the real repo — sandboxes only, cleaned up.
118	- A `fail` needs reproduced evidence; unreproduced findings are downgraded. When you (the Lead) adjudicate a confirmed `fail` at Steps 4–5, apply the **self-confound gate** first — rule out the probe's own provision commands, sandbox reuse, or an earlier probe's mutation as the cause before the finding stands.
119	- Never "execute" an irreversible/outward-facing plan step (push/deploy/send) — analyze it.

Merged arm: when the source IS the plan itself (Part 1 carries the decision record — the plan is its own source of truth; `--spec` defaults to the plan), the lens reads Part-1→Part-2 coverage: every Part-1 requirement/decision maps to a Part-2 phase/task. Split absence arms: an issue whose `## Evidence artifacts` section is absent ⇒ the join is **vacuous** for that issue (the `touched-doc-fact-coverage` vacuity pattern — nothing to join is a pass, not a finding); an issue that is **unreachable** (gh/network/auth failure, incl. an exogenous account flip) ⇒ a **named unverified note** identifying that issue in the report — never silent, never vacuous.
- **consistency-placeholders** — TBD/TODO/vague steps, name/signature drift, contradictions.
- **dependency-feasibility** — assumed interfaces/deps/tools exist; ordering is sound.
- **intent-vs-plan** — fires on either intent heading (`## Commander's Intent` or `## AI-Commander's Intent`): each End-state condition individually checkable (else Major) and mapped to ≥1 claiming phase (else Major); collectively sufficient for the Purpose (else Major `needsDecision`). An `## AI-Commander's Intent` block is intent-present and judged identically, plus one Minor note recommending the human upgrade path (`/war-strategy <plan>`); a plan with **neither** heading passes with a Minor note recommending the intent interview — never Major.

## Drift-guard spine probes (run every red-team)
Four universal doctrine probes the Lead runs on every plan (vacuous when the plan has no matching feature; none skipped under `--fast`), enforcing ADR 0025's drift-guard discipline. **Not** members of the `SPINE` array — Lead-run like the backstop-legitimacy check (see [backstop-legitimacy.md](backstop-legitimacy.md)):
- **`unguarded-new-mirror`** — analyzed. Every new inline mirror of a canonical export a plan adds (a `const` in `workflow-template.js` re-declaring `HARD_ESCALATION_REASONS` / a `landDecision` set / a roster helper) must ship a matching **mirror-registry** row in `workflow-template.test.mjs` in the same task; a mirror with no row is a plan defect (`needsDecision`). Prove by grepping the plan's file list — an added `const` with no registry-row edit in the same task is the fail.
- **`default-flip-old-absent`** — executed. Every default-flip / scope-narrow task's gate must assert the OLD value **absent** across every enumerated surface, not just NEW-present. Prove in a sandbox: leave one stale surface carrying the old value and run the gate; a still-green gate is the defect (`NEW-present` alone is the recorded failure mode).
- **`guard-split-deps-edge`** — analyzed. Every drift guard a plan authors must ride in the **same task** as the fact it guards, or — when split into a different task of the same phase — carry a `deps` edge onto the task authoring that fact; **same wave is insufficient**, because every task worktree is cut from one frozen phase base, so the split guard is red by construction at its own base. Scope is wider than `unguarded-new-mirror`: *any* split drift guard counts — prose mirrors and doc-guard tests included, not only inline `const` mirrors. Prove by reading the plan's per-task `Files:`/`deps:` lists — a guard task with no `deps` edge onto the fact-authoring task is the fail (`needsDecision`), grilled until the plan adds the edge, merges the two tasks, or moves the guard a phase later. Vacuous when the plan splits no guard away from its fact; not skipped under `--fast` (ADR 0025 Consequences).
- **`touched-doc-fact-coverage`** — analyzed. Every task whose `Files:` rewrites a doc must show the **guard / de-mirror / defer** choice for each fact the doc renders authoritative that is derivable from a machine-readable in-repo source (a config default, a manifest field, an enum member, a version slot — never prose claims generally): a **guard** (drift test binding the doc value to its source by extraction + equality), a **de-mirror** (the doc points at the canonical source instead of restating its value), or an **explicit defer** (a legitimacy-complete `## Deferred validations (backstops)` row naming runner + timing — never a prose waiver). Prove by reading the plan's per-task `Files:` lists and slices — a doc-rewriting task restating such a fact with none of the three is the fail (`needsDecision`), grilled until the plan guards, de-mirrors, or explicitly defers. Vacuous when no task rewrites a doc or the touched docs carry no such facts; not skipped under `--fast` (ADR 0025's touched-doc amendment; authoring twin: `/war-strategy` §3 rule 8).

## Bespoke probe catalog (derive from the plan's features)
Add one probe per matching feature (edit the scaffold's array or pass `args.probes`):

| Plan feature | Probe `name` | `technique` | Prompt gist |
|---|---|---|---|
| before/after edit snippet | `snippet-fidelity` | analyzed | "Confirm each **anchor/'before'** snippet (the text an edit attaches to) appears VERBATIM in the live file; report drift + the actual text. The plan's proposed **after**-state is its deliverable — EXPECTED absent, **never** report it." |
| code block + test block | `tests-run` | executed | "Extract the module + test to a temp dir, run the test runner, report the pass/fail counts." |
| shell command + expected output | `command-diff` | executed | "Run the command in a sandbox; diff actual vs the stated Expected." |
| cited line numbers | `anchor-check` | analyzed | "Confirm each cited line number points where the plan says." |
| "no X → today's behavior" baseline | `baseline-repro` | executed | "Reproduce the baseline in a sandbox and confirm the claimed equivalence." |
| new dependency / tool | `dep-resolves` | executed | "Confirm the dep/tool resolves or installs in a sandbox." |
| multi-file edit ordering | `edits-compose` | executed | "Apply all edits to a scratch copy in order; confirm they compose and the result builds." |
| per-task merge-commit anchor (`<merge>^1`, `--first-parent` per-task diff, post-merge three-dot floor base) | `ff-topology` | executed | "In a **fresh `git init` synthetic repo** (never a copy of `repo` — nothing in `repo` is read or run), build WAR's real integration topology: base commit → integration branch → ≥2 'task' integrations done as **fast-forward** merges (a linear single-parent chain — NO per-task merge commit) → one final `--no-ff` phase-land merge. Then evaluate EVERY plan clause that anchors per-task evidence on merge topology against that fixture: a clause that errors, resolves the wrong commit (`^1` on a single-parent tip walks to the previous commit, under-populating the changed-file set), or degenerates to an empty diff (post-merge `<integration>...<task>` is always empty once the task tip is an ancestor) is **topology-void** → Major, with the fixture output as evidence. **Provision-exempt:** build and evaluate the fixture even if repo provisioning failed or was skipped — this probe never touches the repo copy, so a provision failure never converts it to warn-and-skip. **Vacuous pass:** if on reading the plan no clause actually anchors per-task evidence on merge topology (a false-positive token trigger — e.g. `^1` inside an unrelated code block), return `status:\"pass\"` with `findings:[]` — never invent a clause to evaluate." |

For a plan with **no runnable artifacts** (a design doc/PRD), drop the executed probes; coverage, consistency, feasibility, and ambiguity (`needsDecision`) carry the verification.
The **`ff-topology`** row is **mandatory when triggered** and **`--fast`-proof** (it mirrors the SKILL.md Step 2 rule; the presence-pair guard in [`../assets/workflow-scaffold.test.mjs`](../assets/workflow-scaffold.test.mjs) pins the pair). It takes **precedence over** the no-runnable-artifacts executed-drop above: its fixture is a self-contained synthetic repo, so a `design-doc`/`prd` that anchors on per-task merge topology still runs it.

## Scope-lock, attestation & coverage (foreign-cwd defense)
`/red-team` is routinely launched from project X's session to verify project Y's plan (`--repo` ≠ cwd). A probe agent's ambient cwd + CLAUDE.md + memory **overpower** explicit path args, so prevention alone is insufficient (drift survived absolute paths in the 2026-06-19 incident). The hardening is defense-in-depth:
- **Scope-lock preamble** — the scaffold prepends a hard preamble to **every** probe (spine *and* bespoke) and confirm: ignore the session cwd, the only subject is the fingerprinted plan + `repo`, executed probes work in a throwaway *copy* of `repo`, analyzed probes restrict reads to `repo`, and STOP if the opened plan's title differs. **Bespoke probe authors:** you get this for free, but still write your gist to name the absolute `repo`/`planFile`.
- **Provision step (executed probes)** — when the Lead passes a `provision` list (the pinned, repo-derived setup commands — see Part B's `provision.mjs` / setup-scout), the scope-lock additionally directs every **executed** probe to run those commands **in the sandbox copy, before the baseline**, bringing the tree to a gate-ready state (submodules, dependency install, …). Provisioning is environment setup, not the artifact under test: a **failing** provision step is an env-gap → `status:"warn"` + a note, and is **never** a red/fail verdict (a broken environment must not be mis-scored as a broken plan). Stamp the note finding `envGap: true`; the gate demotes it to a Minor note (`../assets/red-team-gate.mjs` `classify()`), so the enforcement is gate-side and typed, not prompt-trust alone. An empty/absent list adds nothing (back-compat); analyzed read-only probes never provision.
- **Anchor attestation** — every probe must report `read_anchor` (what it read); the gate discards off-target results. This is the layer that catches drift even when the preamble fails.
- **`INCOMPLETE` verdict** — the gate returns `CLEARED | CLEARED-WITH-NOTES | ADJUDICATED | BLOCKED | INCOMPLETE`. `INCOMPLETE` whenever a probe was off-target, dropped, or never ran; the gate **never** returns `CLEARED` on incomplete coverage, and `INCOMPLETE` outranks every other arm including `ADJUDICATED`. The Lead re-runs the off-target/dropped probes before any other verdict can settle.
- **Pre/post ref-diff escape guard (executed probes)** — the Lead runs [`../assets/assert-no-repo-escape.sh`](../assets/assert-no-repo-escape.sh) twice: `--repo <repo> --snapshot <abs-file>` immediately before launching the Workflow (an absolute path outside the target's tree; exit 1 there means residue or dirt **predates** this run and must be resolved, never baselined over; pre-existing gitignored residue is the exception — it is recorded in the snapshot, never refused), and `--repo <repo> --baseline <that file>` after it returns and before the gate (0 = clean; 1 = an escape — a stray working-tree file, a **new non-allowlisted gitignored file** measured against the snapshot's recorded ignored file set (including a new file inside a directory the snapshot already listed files under), a junk sandbox ref, or any `refs/heads/`/`refs/tags/` ref added, removed, or SHA-moved since the snapshot; 2 = a git/infra error or unreadable or zero-byte baseline, never a pass). Without `--baseline` the ref half is only the junk-**name** heuristic that a probe-invented name slips, and the gitignored half does not run at all. An exit 1 routes the verdict through the self-confound gate, **action-provenance first** ([../SKILL.md](../SKILL.md) Step 4): a probe-authored or unresolved delta is a real escape and forbids `CLEARED` until containment re-runs the guard clean *with* `--baseline`, while a delta cleared as foreign — another session's or worktree's ref in a shared ref store, or an ignored file another session wrote inside the window — is recorded and does not block `CLEARED` (an ignored path of unsettled provenance is moved aside, never deleted); an exit 2 carries no delta to triage — fix the named git/infra fault and re-run the guard. Both nonzero codes forbid `CLEARED` until the guard is settled. So a probe that escaped its sandbox (the recorded cwd-reset / bare-push shape) is caught by **detection** even when the SCOPE-LOCK **prevention** preamble failed. This is the ratified replacement for the previously-deferred execution harness (ADR 0033); a full probe-confinement jail was a rejected non-goal — the post-run guard closes the trust gap without one.

## Schemas
`FINDINGS` (per probe) and `CONFIRM` (per adversarial-confirm) are defined in the scaffold. `FINDINGS` has a **required** `read_anchor: { resolved_path, plan_title }` — what the probe ACTUALLY read; the gate validates it against the run's **fingerprint** (`{ absPath, titleLine, tokens }`, computed by the Lead from the absolute `planFile` and passed in `args.fingerprint`). A probe whose `read_anchor` does not match the fingerprint is **off-target**: its findings are discarded and it counts as a coverage failure. Shape of a finding:
```jsonc
{ severity: "Critical" | "Major" | "Minor",
  needsDecision: false,          // true = a hole to grill the user on
  deliverableAbsence: false,     // true ONLY when the 'absent' symbol is mapped by coverage-vs-source to a plan task — the gate never blocks on it
  adjudicated: false,            // Lead-stamped at grill time (never probe-set): this blocker/needsDecision is patched but not re-verified. Typed, strict === true; scanned only over the blockers+needsDecision union, so an unstamped Minor never holds the verdict
  claim: "what the plan asserts",
  reality: "what red-team found",
  evidence: "reproduced proof — error output, diff, transcript",
  fix: "suggested resolution",
  planRef: "Task/Step/line" }
```

**Precondition vs deliverable (analyzed probes — shared `preconditionRule` in the scaffold).** A plan *proposes* changes; it has not run. Analyzed probes verify only that the plan's **preconditions** hold against the live repo (the anchor/insertion-point text each edit attaches to exists verbatim, assumed-existing files/symbols/signatures are present, the edits would apply and compose). The plan's proposed new code, new tests, comment edits, and version bumps are its **deliverable** — expected absent, so their finding-shape splits two ways:
- **precondition-missing → a real finding** (a missing/renamed anchor, a false claim about *existing* code, a wrong signature, a drifted line number, an internal contradiction, edits that would not compose).
- **after-state-not-yet-present → NEVER a finding** ("the proposed line/version/test isn't in the repo yet" — that is the expected pre-execution baseline, not a defect).

**Artifact-kind grading (all probes — `futureWorkRule` in the scaffold, ADR 0032).** The precondition/deliverable split above generalizes across probe modes by **`artifactKind`** (`impl-plan` / `tdd-plan` / `design-doc` / `prd`; the Lead classifies it in the pre-flight and threads it in `args.artifactKind` — see [../SKILL.md](../SKILL.md) Step 2; absent ⇒ `impl-plan`, the suppression-safe default). For an `impl-plan` or `tdd-plan`, a claimed-but-unbuilt symbol / test / file is the expected deliverable baseline — **never a finding** — on **executed** probes too, not just analyzed ones; for a `tdd-plan` specifically, a shipped test running **red pre-implementation is `status:"pass"`**, not a defect. The retained-findings carve-out is unchanged: a false claim about *existing* code, a missing anchor, a wrong signature, a drifted line, or an internal contradiction still blocks.

**Deliverable-absence flag (`deliverableAbsence` on a finding).** A probe sets `deliverableAbsence: true` **only** when the 'absent' symbol it flags is mapped by `coverage-vs-source` to a plan task (the plan promises to add it). The gate never counts a `deliverableAbsence:true` finding as a blocker, regardless of severity or probe status — it keys on the typed flag alone, doing no `reality`-string parsing (the gate stays pure). This kills the recorded 16-false-findings `BLOCKED` misfire at the gate layer.

## Severity & gate (enforced by [`../assets/red-team-gate.mjs`](../assets/red-team-gate.mjs))
- **Critical** — provably false in a way that breaks execution (test fails, edit won't apply, file/symbol absent). Blocks **only when the parent probe's `status` is not `"pass"`** (i.e. `warn`, `fail`, or absent). A Critical from a `status:"pass"` probe is a confirmation artifact, not a defect — it does not block.
- **Major** — real defect or coverage gap → wrong/incomplete results. Same status-aware rule: blocks only when probe `status !== "pass"`.
- **Minor** — cosmetic/robustness. Auto-note; auto-fix when unambiguous. Not affected by probe status.
- **`needsDecision`** — an underspecified hole (an ambiguity with >1 non-equivalent resolution) → grill the user, at any severity. **Always blocks, regardless of probe `status`.** Probe agents set `needsDecision:true` on any such finding.
- **Verdict:** `CLEARED` (no blockers/holes/minors) · `CLEARED-WITH-NOTES` (minors only) · `ADJUDICATED` (every open blocker/hole is patched and Lead-stamped, at least one of them; distinct from a clear — no probe re-proof was run) · `BLOCKED` (an open blocker/hole carrying no stamp) · `INCOMPLETE` (coverage gap — an off-target, dropped, or never-ran probe; re-run before any other verdict).

> **Two-contract summary.** (1) *Probe side* — a finding is a DEFECT only; claims that check out are NOT recorded; a clean probe returns `status:"pass"` with `findings:[]`. (2) *Gate side* — `probeStatus !== "pass"` (warn/fail/absent) still blocks for Critical/Major; `needsDecision` always blocks; only literal `"pass"` demotes a Critical/Major to non-blocker.
>
> _Pinned by the **D7 drift-guard** in [`../assets/red-team-gate.test.mjs`](../assets/red-team-gate.test.mjs): it asserts this two-contract sentence is present in both this file and the CONTRACTS comment in [`../assets/workflow-scaffold.js`](../assets/workflow-scaffold.js), and that `'pass'` is the **only** status demoting a Critical/Major — removing either surface, or widening the demoting set, turns the guard red._

## Report template → `docs/red-team/YYYY-MM-DD-<plan-slug>.md`
```markdown
# Red Team — <plan> (<date>)
**Verdict:** CLEARED | CLEARED-WITH-NOTES | ADJUDICATED | BLOCKED | INCOMPLETE — <one line>
**Rounds:** <integer>
<!-- Cumulative grill sweeps: the Step-1 seed + this run's sweeps. Strict form — the next run's seeding re-reads exactly this line; an integer, nothing else. -->

## Attack surface
Spine: <6 lenses>. Bespoke: <probes run>. Executed in sandbox: <which>.
Fallback: <none | analyzed-agent fallback engaged (sticky pin); probes run on general-purpose: names from the dispatchedOn/fallbackEngaged result stamps>.

## Executed proof
- <what ran> → <result, e.g. "tests 20/20 green on Node v26"; "10/10 edits apply">

## Findings
### Critical / Major / Minor
- [<severity>] <claim> → <reality>. Evidence: <…>. Resolution: <patch applied / accepted>.

## Resolutions applied (grill decisions)
- <finding> → <decision> → <plan ref patched>

## Adjudications
<!-- Machine-readable: the WAR Lead reads these rows and threads them into the auditor prompts (auditPrompt() and the gate-audit seats). Version precedence: task instruction > red-team adjudication > plan body literal. Leave empty (or omit) when no authoritative value was adjudicated — an empty block is byte-identical no-op for the auditor.
     Every row carries its OWN provenance token — `operator-ratified (<date>)` or `AI-declared` — never a block-level marker: one run can mix operator rulings with Lead self-adjudication (--afk) in the same report (ADR 0014's heading-level provenance, taken to per-row grain; ADR 0043 Decision 5).
     Carve-out granularity, when a row excludes a registry/both-surfaces-pinned span from a shrink: THE EXTRACTION'S READ IS THE CARVE-OUT — it covers exactly the bytes that row's drift-guard extraction actually reads. Ordered/positional-key regions are atomic; unread residue stays shrink-eligible; the rationale is bounded to runtime prompt strings and never transfers to a standing-doc card span. See docs/adr/0043-adjudicated-clear-distinct-terminal-verdict.md § Carve-out granularity. -->
- <adjudicated literal> supersedes <plan-body literal it replaces> — <plan ref / reason> — <operator-ratified (<date>) | AI-declared>

## Residual risk
- <minor notes / accepted assumptions>

## Route upstream
<!-- Only on a route-upstream terminal (gate emitted `routeUpstream: true`); omit otherwise. Doctrine + block template: skills/red-team/references/loop-budget.md. -->
**Regrill:** `/war-strategy <abs plan path>` — run the interview on the agenda below; it patches the plan.
**Agenda (residual questions):**
- <the unsettled decision — its non-equivalent resolutions, and what the gate saw>

**Re-entry:** `/red-team <abs plan path> [--repo <path>]` — after the regrill; the fresh run seeds its cumulative count from this report's `**Rounds:**` line.
```

## Safety
- Never mutate the repo's source or run the plan against the real repo — sandboxes only, cleaned up.
- A `fail` needs reproduced evidence; unreproduced findings are downgraded. When you (the Lead) adjudicate a confirmed `fail` at Steps 4–5, apply the **self-confound gate** first — rule out the probe's own provision commands, sandbox reuse, or an earlier probe's mutation as the cause before the finding stands.
- Never "execute" an irreversible/outward-facing plan step (push/deploy/send) — analyze it.

Check this package's required resource/import/reference closure, invocation identity, and absence of a development-checkout fallback. This is standalone package completeness, not the complete cross-host sharing/parity requirement the operator deferred. Reject missing required runtime files and escaping resource paths. Record source revision and built artifact identity without requiring the Claude package to share this experimental release.

- Exercise the package after relocation using deterministic fixtures; remove a required asset and alter an invocation to demonstrate those checks fail. Confirm the role instructions used at runtime are the intended packaged ones.

- Provide an explicitly enabled actual-host diagnostic over disposable known-clean and seeded-defect targets, including a real analysis attempt, an executed proof and applicable independent confirmation. Retain input/output evidence and inspect whether the intended work occurred. A missing permission/profile/runtime or skipped live test is unavailable evidence, never a pass. Source/package checks must work without live credentials; a default skip cannot satisfy B1. The actual-host test file must also contain always-on offline cases proving the diagnostic entrypoint loads and exercises its control/result handling with a fake executable, including a missing or unusable result. Its entire file may not skip when live calls are disabled. Task 2 and Task 3 acceptance commands include this file, so absence, syntax/import failure, or broken diagnostic wiring fails source acceptance; these offline checks still do not count as a real host observation.
